title: Hawai'i wildfires Kilohana temporary housing project
description: Nate Wallerstedt, Chief Project Management & Development Branch, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers St. Paul District, discusses the Kilohana temporary housing project for the Hawai'i wildfires disaster response and recovery mission.
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Honolulu District

transcript.text: The Corps of Engineers received a mission from the Federal Emergency Management Agency
to prepare a 169 unit temporary housing site.
We're grading the land, installing utilities and leveling site in preparation for installation
of the units.
The site sits on 34 acres and we're calling it Kielohana, which stands for Lookout Point,
based on the beautiful view.
So the site sits on hard rock, so the contractor will blast to break that rock up.
Once we're done blasting the contractor will process that rock into aggregate that will
be used later to level the site.
Once the site's graded, the contractor will install utilities such as power, sewer and
water and then level the pads for installation of the housing units.
We anticipate the contractor having to blast several times a week in the afternoons between
1 and 4 pm.
We anticipate some temporary impacts to traffic during construction due to increased truck traffic.
However, our contractor will do their best to minimize any disruptions to the community.
Due to the size and complexity of the project, we expect construction to last six months.
Once complete, we will turn the site over to FEMA and they'll install the housing units
on the site.
I'm proud to be part of this team and mission and help the survivors of Mallory recover from
the wildfires.
